_about: Prices set by a public body (or, for Citi Bike, posted by the operator under its city contract). Each is the same product at every date, so a change in the number is a change in price. 'steps' lists the price in effect from each date; checked against the source on 'verified'. Add a step only when the source confirms it.

items.label: Subway and local bus fare
items.quote: The base fare for subways, local buses, and Access-A-Ride will increase 10 cents, from $2.90 to $3.
items.note: Effective Jan. 4, 2026. A rider who pays for 12 rides in seven days rides free for the rest of the week; MTA says no one pays more than $35 a week at the base fare.

items.label: Express bus fare
items.quote: The express bus base fare will increase from $7 to $7.25.

items.label: Verrazzano-Narrows and other major MTA crossings
items.source: MTA Bridges and Tunnels toll rates
items.quote: All toll rates will increase 7.5% at all facilities. (mta.info/fares2025)
items.note: The same rate applies at the RFK, Throgs Neck and Bronx-Whitestone bridges and the Queens Midtown and Hugh L. Carey tunnels. $6.94 times 1.075 is $7.46. Drivers without a New York E-ZPass pay $12.03 by mail.

items.label: Congestion relief zone toll
items.quote: $9 during the peak period and $2.25 during the overnight period.
items.note: Unchanged since the toll began on Jan. 5, 2025. The MTA says it rises to $12 in 2028.

items.label: Water and sewer, typical single-family home
items.source: NYC Water Board and Department of Environmental Protection
items.quote: An increase of 6.0% to the metered and unmetered water and wastewater rates
items.note: Rates change each July 1: +3.7% in 2025, +6.0% in 2026. Dollar amounts are DEP's typical single-family bill; the fiscal 2027 figure is DEP's proposal, $1,224 times the adopted 6.0%.

items.label: New York City minimum wage
items.source: New York State Department of Labor
items.quote: On January 1, 2027, New York's minimum wage will stay the same.
items.note: $17.00 since Jan. 1, 2026, and staying there in 2027.

items.label: Citi Bike annual membership
items.source: Citi Bike (Lyft), 2026 price change notice. The operator's own posted price, not a government source.
items.note: Shown only from the 2026 change: the earlier price was not confirmed on a Citi Bike page, so no change is computed. E-bike time for members went to 27 cents a minute on Jan. 5, 2026, from 25 cents.

stock.label: Market-rate
stock.rule: No cap. Landlord and tenant set the rent at each new lease and renewal.

stock.label: Rent stabilized
stock.rule: Renewals capped by the Rent Guidelines Board: 3% (one-year lease) for leases starting Oct. 1, 2025, then 0% for leases starting Oct. 1, 2026.

stock.label: NYCHA public housing
stock.rule: Tenants generally pay about 30 percent of household income, so rent follows income, not the market.

stock.label: Other regulated (Mitchell-Lama and others)
stock.rule: Set by each program's own rules.

stock.label: Rent controlled
stock.rule: A separate state formula for apartments with tenants in place since before 1971.

acs.note: Census ACS 1-year, New York city, median contract rent (B25058): $1,624 in 2023, $1,695 in 2024. The 2025 figure is scheduled for Oct. 29, 2026.
